confirmed.statement: S1 explicitly states: "Participants were randomly assigned to one of three AI collaboration models:". Figure S1 also labels the three Day 2 modes "Random Group Assignment".
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Theoretical Background and Experimental Design, paragraph beginning "On Day 2"; PDF p. 20 (SI p. 4), Figure S1.

confirmed.statement: The assignment is to individual students in a classroom exercise within an elective course; students receive an ID and group and submit their own story, supporting the individual unit and field_rct coding.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, experimental design; PDF p. 18 (SI p. 2), A.1 Participants; PDF pp. 24-25 (SI pp. 8-9), B.1 Steps 1, 4, and 6.

confirmed.statement: The assigned assistant is ChatGPT 3.5, identified as a language model. Participants use it during their own story production under the assigned rules; separate evaluators subsequently rate the stories with identities and collaboration modes hidden.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Day 2 procedure; PDF p. 8, Limitations; PDF p. 19 (SI p. 3), A.1 Day 2 Task, Recruitment of Evaluators, and Evaluation.

confirmed.statement: Human Confirmation is T1 / instruction Group B: ChatGPT handles ideation, outlining, writing, and editing; participants prompt, accept or request regeneration, and may not introduce their own ideas.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 18 (SI p. 2), A.1 Experiment Design; PDF pp. 26-27 (SI pp. 10-11), B.2.1; PDF p. 48 (SI p. 32), Table S4 group labels.

confirmed.statement: Human Creativity is T2 / instruction Group A: participants ideate and outline without ChatGPT, then prompt and review AI drafting and editing without adding ideas or directly writing/editing the text.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 18-19 (SI pp. 2-3), A.1 Experiment Design; PDF pp. 28-29 (SI pp. 12-13), B.2.2; PDF p. 48 (SI p. 32), Table S4 group labels.

confirmed.statement: Copilot is T3 / instruction Group C: participants and ChatGPT collaborate iteratively at every stage, with participants allowed to contribute ideas, write passages, edit, and request suggestions or feedback.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 19 (SI p. 3), A.1 Experiment Design; PDF pp. 30-31 (SI pp. 14-15), B.2.3; PDF p. 48 (SI p. 32), Table S4 group labels.

confirmed.statement: The randomized comparisons are between different AI collaboration configurations. Copilot permits collaboration throughout; the overall-quality regressions use Human Confirmation as the reference, as the form explains.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, experimental design; PDF pp. 30-31 (SI pp. 14-15), B.2.3; PDF p. 51 (SI p. 35), Table S7 note.

confirmed.statement: The within-person sequence is fixed: all participants write without AI on Day 1 and with AI on Day 2. The form correctly treats the no-AI comparisons as before_after; criterion 1 is supported by randomization between the Day 2 modes.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Day 1 and Day 2 procedures; PDF pp. 19-20 (SI pp. 3-4), A.1 and Figure S1; PDF p. 24 (SI p. 8), B.1 prohibition on Day 1 AI use.

confirmed.statement: GPT-4o classifies story genres and text-embedding-3-large supplies embeddings for similarity measurement; neither is the writing assistant assigned to participants.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, assigned ChatGPT 3.5 assistant; PDF p. 6, Content Diversity; PDF p. 16, Figure 4C caption.

confirmed.statement: S2 is an ancillary comparison of separately administered ChatGPT DAT tests with participants' baseline DAT scores; the form correctly does not call it randomized assignment to AI assistance.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Discussion, second finding; PDF p. 19 (SI p. 3), A.1 Day 1 Task.

summary: The PDF explicitly supports random assignment to three ChatGPT 3.5 collaboration modes for participants' own story writing. The form correctly identifies the fixed Day 1 no-AI/Day 2 AI order, so criterion 1 holds for comparisons between the Day 2 modes.
